conflict_topics: seat reservation vs. physical presence (tissue packet)
who should occupy the disputed seat / timing of yielding
safety and aisle obstruction vs. urgency to eat
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers state concrete practical constraints (spill risk, aisle blocking, time estimates), which grounds the dispute in real trade-offs.
Positions are repeated several times (A repeatedly demands seat; B repeatedly gives remaining time), but repetition is limited and informative.
Observable environment updates (bowl levels, seat availability, TAKE_SEAT/LEAVE_SEAT actions) keep the dialogue well-grounded.

Minor transcript oddity: Agent D attempts to TAKE_SEAT disputed_seat while already occupying the alternative seat; the transcript explicitly notes the failed attempt, which is handled as an observable action rather than ungrounded speech.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent B finished and left the disputed seat; Agent A then took the seat (Agent D had taken an alternative seat earlier and did not occupy the disputed seat). The incompatibility was removed by B's withdrawal/finish and the subsequent physical taking of the seat by A.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A claims the tissue packet reserves the seat and demands B stand; Agent B explicitly rejects that claim and insists they need the seat to finish their bowl (about eight minutes). Agent C warns about aisle obstruction. Clear opposing positions about who should occupy the disputed seat and whether a tissue packet reserves it.

Two minutes later, Agent A presses B to stand now despite spill/aisle risk; Agent B reiterates refusal and gives a time estimate (~six more minutes). Substantive disagreement about whether B must vacate persists unchanged.

After two more minutes Agent A again demands B stand immediately; B reports bowl one-third full and requests ~four more minutes, promising to stand when finished. Positions remain in direct conflict with no settlement.

A new seat opens and Agent D takes it, but the disputed seat issue between A and B remains unresolved (B still eating and refusing to stand). The availability/timing of an alternative seat changes dynamics but does not settle the incompatibility over the disputed seat.

B finishes and leaves the disputed seat (removing B vs A incompatibility). A expects to take it, but Agent D attempts to take the disputed seat as well (and verbally claims it). Transcript notes D could not take it because they already occupy the alternative seat; the attempted competing claim to the seat creates a new conflict between A and D. The original conflict with B is resolved, but a contest over who will now occupy the seat remains.

Agent A physically takes the disputed seat (observable TAKE_SEAT). With B already left and D occupying the alternative seat (and not ultimately occupying the disputed seat), there is no remaining substantive disagreement about seat occupancy.

substantive_insights: The core tension is a norms clash: whether a placeholder (tissue packet) legitimately reserves a seat versus the practical need for immediate seating.
Practical constraints (risk of spilling, blocking aisle, time remaining to eat) are the decisive factors shaping participants' willingness to yield.

Availability and timing of an alternative seat shifted incentives: D taking the alternative seat removed pressure on B but introduced a brief contest over the now-empty disputed seat; ultimately physical actions and timing (B finishing, A taking the seat) resolved the dispute rather than negotiation.
